calls.head: Expect the Sabres to have the puck more
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Sabres have been around the middle of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Sabres’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Quinn sparks the Sabres back from two down
paras: Ryan Donato and Tyler Bertuzzi scored three and a half minutes apart early in the first to put the Blackhawks up 2-0. Jack Quinn got the Sabres on the board five minutes later, and Tage Thompson made it 2-2 early in the second. Oliver Moore restored the Hawks’ lead late in the period, but they didn’t score again. Rasmus Dahlin tied it 3-3 for Buffalo early in the third, and Jiří Kulich put the Sabres ahead for good with less than seven minutes left.

The Sabres carried the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 28-15, and got the result to match. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 12 saves for the Sabres, and Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Alex Vlasic had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Sabres moved to 1-1-0 and climbed out of last place in the NHL, while the Blackhawks dropped to 0-3-0, still last in the NHL.
